about: Inazio Urruzola farms the slopes beneath Mount Hernio, the limestone peak that rises over the hill village of Alkiza in Gipuzkoa, inland from San Sebastián. The family farmstead is said to date to 1348, when it was an apple press for cider, and to have passed down eleven generations as the orchards gave way to vines. Alongside the winery, the family runs a restaurant serving traditional Basque tasting menus, in a building inspired by the sculptor Jorge Oteiza.

Naturala Hernio is a special bottling named for the mountain that shelters the vineyards, which sit around 1,000 feet above sea level, high for txakoli, and catch the breezes from the Bay of Biscay. As with the estate’s other wines, the grapes are farmed sustainably and picked by hand. The name suggests a natural, low-intervention approach, but the producer’s technical details for this cuvée were not available. Expect citrus, white flowers and ripe tropical fruit, with white peach and apple on the palate.
